children: Indian equity indices ended lower for the fourth consecutive session on September 3, giving up early gains as buying in media, realty and banking stocks was outweighed by selling in auto, IT and pharma names.

The markets opened higher amid positive global cues and softer crude oil prices, with the Nifty reclaiming the 24,000 mark in early trade. However, gains failed to sustain as the session progressed, with profit-taking dragging the index below 23,900 after the Closing Auction Session (CAS).
At close, the Sensex was down 417.49 points or 0.55 percent at 76,152.86, and the Nifty was down 41 points or 0.17 percent at 23,873.45.
The broader market outperformed the main indices with Nifty midcap index rising 0.37 percent and smallcap index advancing 1.2 percent.
Top gainers on Nifty were Adani Ports, Axis Bank, HDFC Bank, Bharat Electronics, Asian Paints, while losers were Tech Mahindra, Cipla, Bajaj Auto, Cipla and M&M.
On the sectoral front auto, FMCG, IT and Pharma down 0.5% each, while Realty index gained 2.5%, Media index up 1.7%, and PSU Bank and Private Bank rose 0.5% each.

More than 180 stocks touched 52-week high including Capri Global, Welspun Corp, RBL Bank, Caplin Labs, Solar Industries, PTC Industries, Sai Life Sciences, Welspun Living, IFCI, among others. Click to View More

Among individual stocks, Autoline Industries shares surged 10% on Rs 100 crore order from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicle, while Inox Wind advanced 5% after securing a 100 MW turnkey order from Indian Oil Corporation.

Page Industries slipped 1.5% after receiving an AED 113.5 million notice from the Dubai Court. Welspun Corp gained over 4% after Jefferies initiated a 'Buy' call with a Rs 3,250 target, while Godrej Consumer shares slipped 3% after CLSA upgraded to Underperform and cut target to Rs 743.
Hexaware Technologies fell 2.3% following the CEO’s resignation, while HUDCO gained 1.4% after signing an MoU with the Bihar government.
The Indian rupee strengthened to a two-month high, ending 48 paise higher at 94.49 per dollar, compared with the previous close of 94.97.
New Listing
Lumino Industries shares ended 35.6% higher at Rs 111.20 after listing at more than 34 percent premium, at Rs 110 per share on the NSE.
Outlook for September 4
Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst at LKP Securities
The Nifty started on a gap-up note but faced resistance near the lower band of the rising channel, triggering selling pressure throughout the day.

On the daily timeframe, a Dark Cloud Cover candlestick pattern has formed, indicating potential weakness in the near term. On the lower end, support is placed at 23,850, below which the index may decline towards 23,700–23,730.
On the higher end, resistance is placed at 24,000. A sustained move above 24,000 would be required to negate the immediate bearish bias.
Siddhartha Khemka - Head of Research, Wealth Management, Motilal Oswal Financial Services

Indian equities are likely to remain under pressure amid elevated crude prices, keeping investor sentiment cautious. Brent crude rose 1.6% to around USD 97/bbl, near its highest levels in over a month, as investors continued to monitor Middle East developments.

Domestic equities ended mixed, with the Nifty 50 declining 0.2%, while the Midcap100 and Smallcap100 gained 0.4% and 1.2%, respectively. The rupee strengthened 67 paise at the open, marking its biggest single-day gain since June.
India’s Services PMI rose to 54.1 in August from 53.3 in July, while employment growth reached a 15-month high.

Banking stocks remained in focus, with both Private Banks and PSU Banks gaining 0.5%. Banks mobilised USD 136.4bn through the RBI’s twin forex swap windows, lifting system liquidity surplus above Rs 6tn and supporting deposit and credit growth, although near-term NIM pressure remains a concern. Investors will track US jobs data and S&P Services & Composite PMI later today, followed by US non-farm payrolls and unemployment data tomorrow.
